summary: The note surveys ten categories of adaptive learning technology introduced in classrooms after September 2023, each illustrated with a named product and launch date. These tools tailor instruction to individual learners through AI, real-time feedback, gamification, data analytics, VR, NLP, and dashboards. The note concludes that education is moving toward more personalized, effective, and engaging experiences.
one_line: Overview of ten adaptive learning technologies, from AI platforms to VR and dashboards, launched since late 2023 to personalize student instruction.
key_facts: NewtonPlus launched its AI-driven learning platform in late 2023, using algorithms to adjust difficulty and content type as a student progresses.
EduGuide Technologies developed a smart tutoring system, released in early 2024, that blends machine learning and cognitive science to give real-time hints, encouragement, or detailed explanations.
Quest2Learn, a game-based learning platform, emerged in mid-2024 with educational games where students complete missions and advance through levels.

LearnFlex Pro, an adaptive learning management system, launched in November 2023 and customizes content based on a student's progress, such as more time on algebra or quicker progress through grammar.
DataEdu, launched in January 2024, collects and analyzes educational data to give teachers insight into individual performance and learning gaps.
VRLearn, described as a pioneer program, debuted in February 2024 and offers adaptive VR scenarios such as walking through the Colosseum or watching cells divide in 3D.
WriteGenius, launched in March 2024, uses natural language processing to give adaptive feedback on grammar, structure, style, and originality.
InterBook, an interactive e-textbook platform, hit the shelves in April 2024 and updates content in real time with assessments adapting to the student's knowledge level.
TeamLearn developed a cloud-based collaboration tool, launched in mid-2024, that supports cooperative learning by adapting to each participant's needs.
ProgressTrack, a personalized learning dashboard, launched in September 2024 and visualizes individual learning data, highlighting strengths and areas needing development.
The note says the technologies were integrated into classrooms post-September 2023.
The note's frontmatter places it under the topic 'Local Education Systems'.
